newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty climbs toward resistance, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty climbs toward resistance, depos ease.

text.p: The Polish zloty edged up to resistance at 1.5 percent from parity in early Monday trade, but has so far failed to cross into intervention territory.

"The market is straddling the new resistance, with no rapid movement in either way expected...but the feeling is the zloty should strengthen further in the direction of two percent (from parity)," said Pawel Gajewski, forex dealer at Creditanstalt.

Some dealers expected the central bank to intervene against the zloty if the local unit firmed past 1.5 percent from parity, while others said the central bank may refrain from currency-buying as long as the market remained balanced.
At 0815 GMT the zloty was quoted at 1.54/1.48 percent from parity, stronger than 1.52/1.32 percent at opening.
It was at 3.2090/00 to the dollar, against 3.2080/150 at 0707 GMT and at 1.8702/22 to the mark, up from 1.8720/55.

Dealers said foreign investor entry into Polish T-bills at Monday's 1.6 billion zloty auction would drive the zloty higher against the basket of currencies despite expectations of a central bank intervention.
On Friday, the central bank staged a small $20 million intervention to knock the zloty below 1.5 percent from parity.
On the money market one-day rates eased below 23 percent on the first day of the June required reserve period as banks let cash out after hoarding funds at the end of last month.
Overnight rates eased to 22.25/22.65 percent from 22.40/23.00 percent at 0630 GMT. Tomorrow/next rates slipped to 22.45/22.60 percent from 22.60/23.15.
